purpose: Backs the no-overclaim check: every capability claim the CLI or README makes must map to at least one check id that passes in the same run.
how_it_is_evaluated: A row is ACTIVE when its `marker` string is found in its `source`.
`source` is a repo-relative file path, or the literal `help` meaning the output of `bin/productteam help`.
An ACTIVE row passes only if every id in `checks` has status pass in this run.

An INACTIVE row (marker absent) is inert: the claim is not being made, so there is nothing to overclaim. Rows for capabilities the mission intends to add are pre-registered this way so they activate the moment the claim appears.
maintenance_rule: Adding a capability claim to README.md or `productteam help` without adding a row here is itself an overclaim. Reviewers should diff this file against README/help changes.

claims.claim: The bare CLI gives an org and engagements overview.
The CLI detects coding runtimes present on the device.
`runtime --check` fails when no usable provider exists.
The default provider is the authenticated Cursor agent CLI, swappable via CONSULT_PROVIDER.
No API keys and no mocks are used.
Engagements with scorer=checks are scored by deterministic contract checks.
`productteam checks` refuses engagements that do not declare scorer=checks.
`productteam score` routes to whichever scorer the engagement declares.
claims.marker: Score via the engagement's declared scorer

claims.claim: `productteam bench` shows the frozen contract, history, and latest scores.
Merge is gated on an authorize-merge file and never uses --admin.
Three first-party skills are runnable from the CLI.
Skills are runnable against any target repo from the README quickstart.
The CLI ships smoke tests.
Organizational memory and org/roles views are reachable.
Every command shown in help exists and is dispatched.
Documented layout paths resolve on disk.
Skills make real provider calls, verified against the engagement tmp projects.
A first-run onboarding entry point exists.
README documents the first run, including onboarding, splash, and agent detection.
A bounded login/splash animation exists and can be opted out of.
The CLI lists every coding agent found on the device, with machine-readable output.
The CLI states its non-goals.
